source.text: Περὶ δὲ ὧν ἐγράψατε, καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ γυναικὸς μὴ ἅπτεσθαι·

records.literal_gloss: Concerning but [the things] which you wrote, good for a man a woman not to touch;

en.L: Now concerning [the things] of which you wrote: "[It is] good for a man not to touch a woman."
en.B: Now about the matters you wrote of. "It is good for a man to have no sexual contact with a woman."
en.R: Now I turn to the things you wrote to me about. Some of you say, "It is good for a man to keep away from sex with a woman."

fr.L: Or, au sujet de ce que vous avez écrit : « [Il est] bon pour un homme de ne pas toucher de femme. »
fr.B: Passons maintenant aux questions dont vous m’avez parlé dans votre lettre. « Il est bon pour un homme de n’avoir aucune relation sexuelle avec une femme. »
fr.R: J’en viens maintenant aux questions que vous m’avez posées dans votre lettre. Certains d’entre vous disent : « C’est bien, pour un homme, de se passer de relations sexuelles avec une femme. »

es.L: Ahora bien, acerca de lo que {{plural_you:escribieron|escribisteis}}: «Bueno [es] para el hombre no tocar mujer».
es.B: Ahora, en cuanto a los asuntos sobre los que {{plural_you:escribieron|escribisteis}}: «Es bueno que el hombre no tenga relaciones sexuales con una mujer».
es.R: Paso ahora a las cosas sobre las que me {{plural_you:escribieron|escribisteis}}. Algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} dicen: «Es bueno que un hombre no tenga relaciones sexuales con una mujer».

sw.L: Basi kuhusu [mambo] mliyoandika: "[Ni] vizuri kwa mwanamume asimguse mwanamke."
sw.B: Basi kuhusu mambo mliyoniandikia: "Ni vizuri mwanamume asikutane kimwili na mwanamke."
sw.R: Sasa nageukia mambo mliyoniandikia. Baadhi yenu mnasema, "Ni vizuri mwanamume ajiepushe kabisa na kufanya ngono na mwanamke."

decisions.choice: the words after the comma quote a saying from the Corinthians' letter, which Paul goes on to answer
alternatives: Paul's own statement, that it is good to stay away from sexual relations, which he then qualifies in verse 2
decisions.reason: Ancient manuscripts have no quotation marks, so where a quotation begins is an editorial judgment; the SBLGNT prints none here. Paul quotes the Corinthians' own sayings elsewhere in the letter and then corrects them ("All things are permitted for me", 6:12; "We all have knowledge", 8:1). Περὶ δὲ ("now concerning") turns to a question from their letter, as it does again in 7:25; 8:1; 12:1 and 16:1. Verses 2-5 then argue against married couples giving up sexual relations, which fits best if the saying came from some in Corinth who held that view. Yet Paul himself says that staying unmarried is good (verses 7-8, 26), so he may also agree with the saying in part.

decisions.choice: touch a woman: have sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: "Touch" was a common polite way of speaking of sexual relations, as in the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 20:6 and Proverbs 6:29. The question is not about marriage as such, which comes up in verse 9, but about sexual relations, including within marriage (verses 3-5).

decisions.choice: a man ... a woman: a male and a female person
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπῳ (from ἄνθρωπος, a human being) stands here against γυναικὸς, so a man is meant. The saying is put generally, but verses 2-5 apply it to husbands and wives.

decisions.choice: Some of you say
decisions.reason: Readable says outright that the words are a saying from Corinth (m1), since quotation marks alone are easy to miss. Literal and Balanced show it with quotation marks.

decisions.choice: have no sexual contact with (B); keep away from sex with (R)
decisions.reason: In modern English "touch" would not be heard as sexual (m2). Literal keeps "touch".

decisions.choice: un homme, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The saying sets a man against a woman (m3), so the noun means a male and takes no inclusive alternative, as in English.

decisions.choice: «...» (L, B); Algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} dicen: «...» (R)
decisions.reason: The Corinthian saying (m1) stands in «» quotation marks, as the slogans of 6:12-13 do, and Readable says who is speaking with the same words as 6:12.

decisions.choice: no tocar mujer (L); no tenga relaciones sexuales con una mujer (B, R)
alternatives: no tocar a una mujer (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Tocar mujer" keeps the Greek picture at Literal; it is a known idiom for sexual relations (m2), which Balanced and Readable say plainly.

decisions.choice: Baadhi yenu mnasema
decisions.reason: As in 6:12 and the English Readable: the Corinthian saying is marked as theirs, so the reader does not take it for Paul's own view; Literal and Balanced use quotation marks only.

decisions.choice: asimguse (L); asikutane kimwili (B); ajiepushe na kufanya ngono (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture "touch"; Balanced uses "kukutana kimwili", the usual decent Swahili expression for sexual relations; Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

source.text: διὰ δὲ τὰς πορνείας ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἐχέτω, καὶ ἑκάστη τὸν ἴδιον ἄνδρα ἐχέτω.

records.literal_gloss: Because of but the sexual immoralities each [man] the wife of himself let him have, and each [woman] the own husband let her have.

en.L: But because of the sexual immoralities, let each [man] have his own wife, and let each [woman] have her own husband.
en.B: But because sexual immorality is all around, each man is to have relations with his own wife. Each woman, too, is to have relations with her own husband.
en.R: But there is a lot of sexual sin around you. So each man should have sex only with his own wife, and each woman only with her own husband.

fr.L: Mais à cause des immoralités sexuelles, que chacun ait sa propre femme, et que chacune ait son propre mari.
fr.B: Mais comme l’immoralité sexuelle est partout, chaque homme doit avoir des relations avec sa propre femme, et chaque femme aussi avec son propre mari.
fr.R: Mais il y a beaucoup de péchés sexuels autour de vous. Alors chaque homme doit avoir des relations sexuelles seulement avec sa femme, et chaque femme seulement avec son mari.

es.L: Pero, a causa de las inmoralidades sexuales, que cada uno tenga su propia mujer, y que cada una tenga su propio marido.
es.B: Pero como la inmoralidad sexual está por todas partes, cada hombre debe tener relaciones con su propia mujer. Y también cada mujer, con su propio marido.
es.R: Pero hay mucho pecado sexual a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} alrededor. Por eso, cada hombre debe tener relaciones sexuales solo con su propia esposa, y cada mujer solo con su propio esposo.

sw.L: Lakini kwa sababu ya uasherati, kila [mwanamume] na awe na mke wake mwenyewe, na kila [mwanamke] na awe na mume wake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Lakini kwa kuwa uasherati umeenea kila mahali, kila mwanamume na akutane kimwili na mke wake mwenyewe, na kila mwanamke vivyo hivyo na mume wake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Lakini dhambi ya ngono imeenea sana mahali mnapoishi. Kwa hiyo kila mwanamume afanye ngono na mke wake tu, na kila mwanamke na mume wake tu.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual relations outside marriage, in all its forms
decisions.reason: πορνείας covers any sexual sin: chapter 5 deals with a man living with his father's wife, and 6:12-20 with men going to prostitutes. The plural points to actual cases, or to the many temptations, in a city like Corinth.

decisions.choice: have a wife, have a husband: have sexual relations with one's own spouse
alternatives: take a wife or a husband: get married
decisions.reason: "Have" a woman or a man can mean to have sexual relations with them (5:1, of the man who "has" his father's wife). Here Paul speaks to married people, as verses 3-5 show, and tells them to keep up sexual relations with each other, not to give them up. Some read it instead as advice to marry, which Paul gives to the unmarried in verse 9.

decisions.choice: each man ... each woman: the same command, in the same words, for both
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to the wife as directly as to the husband, with matching words, ἕκαστος and ἑκάστη, "his own" and "her own". The same balance runs through verses 3-4 and 10-16.

decisions.choice: have relations with (B); have sex only with (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "have" here (m2); Literal keeps the Greek wording. Readable's "only" says what "his own" and "her own" mean.

decisions.choice: sexual sin
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for the same thing.

decisions.choice: chacun ... chacune (L)
decisions.reason: French, like Greek, marks the man and the woman by the form of the pronoun, so Literal needs no brackets for the words the English supplies.

decisions.choice: cada uno ... cada una, no brackets
decisions.reason: The Greek shows man and woman by the ending of "each". Spanish does the same with "cada uno" and "cada una", so Literal needs none of the words the English brackets.

decisions.choice: mujer, marido (L, B); esposa, esposo (R)
decisions.reason: One Greek word means both woman and wife, and Spanish "mujer" does the same, so Literal and Balanced keep "mujer" and "marido" through the chapter; Readable says "esposa" and "esposo", the plainest words for spouses.

decisions.choice: uasherati (L, B); dhambi ya ngono (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili words for porneia in this letter (5:1), used through chapters 6 and 7.

source.text: τῇ γυναικὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἀποδιδότω, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ τῷ ἀνδρί.

records.literal_gloss: To the wife the husband the debt let him pay, likewise and also the wife to the husband.

en.L: Let the husband pay to the wife what is owed, and likewise also the wife to the husband.
en.B: A husband must give his wife what he owes her in marriage, and a wife must do the same for her husband.
en.R: A husband should give his wife what she needs from him in their sexual life, and a wife should do the same for her husband.

fr.L: Que le mari rende à la femme ce qui [lui] est dû, et de même aussi la femme au mari.
fr.B: Le mari doit donner à sa femme ce qu’il lui doit dans le mariage, et la femme doit faire de même envers son mari.
fr.R: Un mari doit donner à sa femme ce dont elle a besoin de lui dans leur vie sexuelle, et une femme doit faire de même pour son mari.

es.L: Que el marido pague a la mujer lo debido, y del mismo modo también la mujer al marido.
es.B: El marido debe dar a su mujer lo que le debe en el matrimonio, y la mujer debe hacer lo mismo con su marido.
es.R: El esposo debe darle a su esposa lo que ella necesita de él en su vida sexual, y la esposa debe hacer lo mismo con su esposo.

sw.L: Mume na amlipe mke kile anachodaiwa, na vivyo hivyo pia mke kwa mume.
sw.B: Mume ampe mkewe kile anachomwia katika ndoa, na mke naye afanye vivyo hivyo kwa mumewe.
sw.R: Mume ampe mkewe kile anachohitaji kutoka kwake katika tendo la ndoa, na mke naye afanye vivyo hivyo kwa mumewe.

decisions.choice: what is owed: the sexual relationship each spouse owes the other
decisions.reason: ὀφειλὴν is a debt or obligation. Between verse 2 and verse 5 ("do not deprive one another") it is plainly a gentle way of speaking about sexual relations. Paul frames them as something given to the other, not taken.

decisions.choice: the obligation runs both ways, equally
decisions.reason: In the world of the time a wife's duty to her husband was taken for granted, and a husband's freedom much greater. Paul gives the husband the duty first and then says the wife has the very same one, ὁμοίως, "likewise".

decisions.choice: what he owes her in marriage (B); what she needs from him in their sexual life (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the idea of something owed and adds "in marriage"; Readable says plainly what is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: kile anachodaiwa (L); kile anachomwia katika ndoa (B)
decisions.reason: "Haki" is kept for righteousness throughout, so the debt is put with the verbs of owing: "kudaiwa" (be owed, L) and "kuwia" (owe someone, B).

decisions.choice: tendo la ndoa
decisions.reason: "Tendo la ndoa" (the act of marriage) is the plain, decent Swahili term for sexual relations between husband and wife.

source.text: ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλὰ ὁ ἀνήρ· ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλὰ ἡ γυνή.

records.literal_gloss: The wife of the own body does not have authority but the husband; likewise and also the husband of the own body does not have authority but the wife.

en.L: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband [does]; and likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife [does].
en.B: The wife does not rule over her own body; her husband does. In the same way, the husband does not rule over his own body; his wife does.
en.R: A wife is not the one in charge of her own body; her husband is. And in the same way, a husband is not the one in charge of his own body; his wife is.

fr.L: La femme n’a pas autorité sur son propre corps, mais le mari ; et de même aussi le mari n’a pas autorité sur son propre corps, mais la femme.
fr.B: La femme ne dispose pas de son propre corps : c’est son mari qui en dispose. De même, le mari ne dispose pas de son propre corps : c’est sa femme qui en dispose.
fr.R: Ce n’est pas la femme qui décide pour son propre corps, c’est son mari. Et de la même façon, ce n’est pas le mari qui décide pour son propre corps, c’est sa femme.

es.L: La mujer no tiene autoridad sobre su propio cuerpo, sino el marido; y del mismo modo tampoco el marido tiene autoridad sobre su propio cuerpo, sino la mujer.
es.B: La mujer no es quien manda sobre su propio cuerpo, sino su marido. Del mismo modo, el marido no es quien manda sobre su propio cuerpo, sino su mujer.
es.R: La esposa no es la que decide sobre su propio cuerpo; decide su esposo. Y, del mismo modo, el esposo no es el que decide sobre su propio cuerpo; decide su esposa.

sw.L: Mke hana mamlaka juu ya mwili wake mwenyewe, bali mume [anayo]; na vivyo hivyo pia mume hana mamlaka juu ya mwili wake mwenyewe, bali mke [anayo].
sw.B: Mke hautawali mwili wake mwenyewe; mumewe ndiye anayeutawala. Vivyo hivyo, mume hautawali mwili wake mwenyewe; mkewe ndiye anayeutawala.
sw.R: Mke si yeye mwenye kauli juu ya mwili wake; mumewe ndiye mwenye kauli. Vivyo hivyo, mume si yeye mwenye kauli juu ya mwili wake; mkewe ndiye mwenye kauli.

decisions.choice: have authority over: have the right to decide about, here in the sexual relationship
alternatives: own, in the sense of property
decisions.reason: ἐξουσιάζει means to have the right or power over something. Paul has used the related word in 6:12 ("I will not be mastered by anything"). In marriage neither partner decides alone about the sexual relationship; each has given the other a claim.

decisions.choice: the husband's body is under his wife's claim, as hers is under his
decisions.reason: That a husband had rights over his wife was a common view. That a wife had rights over her husband's body was not, and the second half of the verse matches the first word for word. Paul's point is the mutual claim, which leads into verse 5.

decisions.choice: rule over (B); be in charge of (R)
decisions.reason: Both put the idea of having the say over something in everyday words; Literal keeps "have authority over".

decisions.choice: sino el marido ... sino la mujer, no brackets
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the verb out after "sino" as naturally as the Greek, so Literal needs no bracketed "[does]".

decisions.choice: mwenye kauli
decisions.reason: "Kuwa na kauli juu ya" (to have the say over) is everyday Swahili for being the one who decides, as the English Readable's "in charge of".

source.text: μὴ ἀποστερεῖτε ἀλλήλους, εἰ μήτι ἂν ἐκ συμφώνου πρὸς καιρὸν ἵνα σχολάσητε τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ πάλιν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἦτε, ἵνα μὴ πειράζῃ ὑμᾶς ὁ Σατανᾶς διὰ τὴν ἀκρασίαν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, that you may devote yourselves to the prayer and again on the same you may be, so that not may tempt you the Satan because of the lack of self-control of you.

en.L: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer, and [that] you may be together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
en.B: Do not refuse each other, unless you both agree to it for a limited time so that you are free for prayer. Then be together again, or Satan may use your lack of self-control to tempt you.
en.R: Do not say no to each other. The only exception is when you both agree to stop for a short time so that you can give that time to prayer. Then come back together. Otherwise Satan may tempt you, because you find it hard to control your desires.

fr.L: Ne vous privez pas l’un l’autre, sauf peut-être d’un commun accord, pour un temps, afin de vous consacrer à la prière, et [afin] que vous soyez de nouveau ensemble, pour que Satan ne vous tente pas à cause de votre manque de maîtrise de soi.
fr.B: Ne vous refusez pas l’un à l’autre, sauf si vous êtes tous deux d’accord, pour un temps limité, afin d’être libres pour la prière. Puis retrouvez-vous, sinon Satan pourrait profiter de votre manque de maîtrise de soi pour vous tenter.
fr.R: Ne vous dites pas non l’un à l’autre. La seule exception, c’est quand vous êtes tous les deux d’accord pour arrêter pendant un peu de temps, afin de donner ce temps à la prière. Ensuite, retrouvez-vous. Sinon Satan pourrait vous tenter, parce que vous avez du mal à maîtriser vos désirs.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se priven|os privéis}} el uno del otro, a no ser quizá de común acuerdo por un tiempo, para {{plural_you:dedicarse|dedicaros}} a la oración, y [que] de nuevo {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} juntos, para que no {{plural_you:los|os}} tiente Satanás a causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} falta de dominio propio.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se nieguen|os neguéis}} el uno al otro, a menos que los dos {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} de acuerdo en hacerlo por un tiempo limitado, para quedar libres para la oración. Después {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a estar juntos, no sea que Satanás se aproveche de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} falta de dominio propio para {{plural_you:tentarlos|tentaros}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:se digan|os digáis}} que no el uno al otro. La única excepción es cuando los dos {{plural_you:están|estáis}} de acuerdo en dejarlo por poco tiempo, para dedicar ese tiempo a la oración. Después {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a estar juntos. Si no, Satanás puede {{plural_you:tentarlos|tentaros}}, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} cuesta controlar {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} deseos.

sw.L: Msinyimane, isipokuwa labda kwa makubaliano kwa muda, ili mjitoe kwa maombi, na [kwamba] mkae pamoja tena, ili Shetani asiwajaribu kwa sababu ya kutokuwa na kiasi kwenu.
sw.B: Msinyimane, isipokuwa mmekubaliana wote wawili kwa muda maalum ili mpate nafasi ya kuomba. Kisha kutaneni tena, Shetani asije akatumia kushindwa kwenu kujizuia ili kuwajaribu.
sw.R: Msikataliane. Mnaweza kufanya hivyo tu pale mnapokubaliana wote wawili kuacha kwa muda mfupi, ili mtumie wakati huo kuomba. Kisha kutaneni tena kama mume na mke. La sivyo Shetani anaweza kuwajaribu, kwa sababu mnaona vigumu kuzizuia tamaa zenu.

decisions.choice: deprive: hold back from the other what is owed, here sexual relations
decisions.reason: ἀποστερεῖτε means to rob or defraud; Paul used it in 6:7-8 of believers cheating one another. Refusing sexual relations is withholding the "debt" of verse 3.

decisions.choice: the one exception has three limits: both agree, it is for a set time, and it is for prayer
decisions.reason: εἰ μήτι ἂν ("unless perhaps") makes the exception hesitant. ἐκ συμφώνου means by mutual agreement, not one partner deciding; πρὸς καιρὸν means for a season, not for good.

decisions.choice: be together again: resume sexual relations
decisions.reason: The phrase means to be in the same place, together. After the time of prayer the couple go back to their normal married life.

decisions.choice: lack of self-control: inability to master one's desires
decisions.reason: ἀκρασίαν is the opposite of self-control (compare verse 9). Paul expects married people to need their sexual relationship, and does not treat this as a fault to be ashamed of.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "devote yourselves to prayer ... be together again"
alternatives: "devote yourselves to fasting and prayer ... come together again"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "fasting and" before "prayer", and some read "come together" for "be together". The shorter text is found in the earliest manuscripts, and the mention of fasting is the kind of addition copyists made (compare Mark 9:29). Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: refuse each other (B); say no to each other (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what depriving means here (m1); Literal keeps "deprive".

decisions.choice: you find it hard to control your desires
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun into a short clause and names what is hard to control.

decisions.choice: el uno al otro, el uno del otro
decisions.reason: The command is to a husband and a wife, two people, so Spanish says "el uno al otro" rather than "unos a otros", which would suggest a group.

decisions.choice: kutaneni tena (B); kutaneni tena kama mume na mke (R)
decisions.reason: "Kukutana" carries on the expression of verse 2 for married relations; "kurudiana" would suggest making up after a quarrel.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ λέγω κατὰ συγγνώμην, οὐ κατ’ ἐπιταγήν.

records.literal_gloss: This but I say according to concession, not according to command.

en.L: But this I say by way of concession, not by way of command.
en.B: What I am saying here is a concession; it is not a command.
en.R: I am allowing this, not ordering you to do it.

fr.L: Mais je dis cela par concession, non par ordre.
fr.B: Ce que je dis là est une concession, ce n’est pas un ordre.
fr.R: Je vous permets cela, je ne vous l’ordonne pas.

es.L: Pero esto [lo] digo a modo de concesión, no a modo de mandato.
es.B: Lo que digo aquí es una concesión, no un mandato.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} permito hacer esto, pero no {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} ordeno.

sw.L: Lakini hili nasema kwa njia ya kuruhusu, si kwa njia ya amri.
sw.B: Ninachosema hapa ni ruhusa; si amri.
sw.R: Ninawaruhusu kufanya hivi, si kwamba ninawaamuru.

decisions.choice: this: the allowance in verse 5 for a time apart for prayer
alternatives: the instruction to marry or to keep up married relations (verse 2)
decisions.reason: τοῦτο most naturally points back to what Paul has just said. He allows a time of abstaining but does not require it; he would not call the married duty of verses 3-4 a mere concession. Some take "this" to cover verse 2 as well, so that marriage itself is allowed rather than commanded; verse 7 might support that.

decisions.choice: concession: something allowed, out of understanding, rather than required
decisions.reason: συγγνώμην means indulgence or allowance, a making room for people. It is set against ἐπιταγήν, an order or command. Paul is not saying he has no authority here; he is saying this point is permitted, not imposed.

decisions.choice: I am allowing this, not ordering you to do it
alternatives: by way of concession, not command
decisions.reason: Readable uses verbs in place of the abstract nouns.

source.text: θέλω δὲ πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἶναι ὡς καὶ ἐμαυτόν· ἀλλὰ ἕκαστος ἴδιον ἔχει χάρισμα ἐκ θεοῦ, ὁ μὲν οὕτως, ὁ δὲ οὕτως.

records.literal_gloss: I wish but all men to be as even myself; but each own has gift from God, the one thus, the other thus.

en.L: But I wish {{gender:all people|all men}} to be as I myself also [am]; but each has {{gender:their|his}} own gift from God, one in this way, another in that way.
en.B: I would like everyone to be as I am. Yet God gives each person a gift of {{gender:their|his}} own, to one this way and to another that.
en.R: I wish everyone could be like me and not be married. But God gives different gifts to different people. One person has one gift, and another person has another.

fr.L: Mais je voudrais que {{gender:tous les humains|tous les hommes}} soient comme moi-même aussi ; mais chacun a de Dieu son propre don, l’un de cette manière-ci, l’autre de cette manière-là.
fr.B: Je voudrais que tout le monde soit comme moi. Mais Dieu donne à chacun un don qui lui est propre, à l’un de cette façon, à l’autre de cette autre façon.
fr.R: Je voudrais que tout le monde puisse être comme moi, sans être marié. Mais Dieu donne des dons différents à des personnes différentes. L’un a un don, et l’autre en a un autre.

es.L: Pero quisiera que {{gender:todos los seres humanos|todos los hombres}} fueran como también yo mismo; pero cada uno tiene su propio don de Dios, uno de esta manera, otro de aquella.
es.B: Me gustaría que todos fueran como yo. Pero Dios da a cada uno su propio don, a uno de una manera y a otro de otra.
es.R: Quisiera que todos pudieran ser como yo y no estar casados. Pero Dios da dones diferentes a personas diferentes. Una persona tiene un don, y otra persona tiene otro.

sw.L: Lakini nataka watu wote wawe kama mimi mwenyewe pia [nilivyo]; lakini kila mmoja ana karama yake mwenyewe kutoka kwa Mungu, mmoja hivi, mwingine hivi.
sw.B: Ningependa kila mtu awe kama nilivyo mimi. Lakini Mungu humpa kila mtu karama yake mwenyewe, mmoja kwa namna hii, mwingine kwa namna ile.
sw.R: Natamani kila mtu angekuwa kama mimi, bila kuoa wala kuolewa. Lakini Mungu huwapa watu karama tofauti. Mtu mmoja ana karama hii, na mwingine ana karama ile.

decisions.choice: as I myself: unmarried, and able to live so without being troubled by desire
decisions.reason: Verse 8 shows that Paul was unmarried when he wrote. Whether he had been married before is not known. He had the right to take a believing wife with him on his travels (9:5) but chose not to.

decisions.choice: gift: a gift of God's grace, here the ability God gives for one's way of life
decisions.reason: χάρισμα is built from the word for grace (1:7). Paul calls his own way of life a gift from God, not an achievement, and says each person has one.

decisions.choice: one this way, another that way: both the unmarried life and married life are gifts from God
alternatives: the unmarried have one gift, and the married have other gifts of other kinds
decisions.reason: The two phrases are left open. In context the most natural reading is that some are given the unmarried life and others married life, so neither group should despise the other. Some read it more broadly, of the many different gifts of chapter 12.

decisions.choice: {{gender:all people|all men}} (L); {{gender:their|his}} (L, B)
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπους here means human beings, women and men; Balanced and Readable say "everyone", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: and not be married
decisions.reason: Readable says what "as I am" refers to (m1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:tous les humains|tous les hommes}} (L); "tout le monde" (B, R); "chacun ... son" without a span (L, B)
decisions.reason: The noun for human beings takes the setting at Literal, as in English. French "chacun" and "son" are already generic, so the English span on "their/his" has no French counterpart.

decisions.choice: don (every level)
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "gift" for this word through the letter: "charisme" is church language and "don spirituel" belongs to another Greek word (12:1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:todos los seres humanos|todos los hombres}} (L); todos, su propio, no span (B)
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the English setting for the noun, as in 2:3. "Todos" alone and "su" (his or her) already cover everyone, so Balanced and the possessive need no span.

decisions.choice: don
decisions.reason: "Don" is the Spanish word for a gift of God's grace, as in Romans 12:6, and is kept for this word through chapters 12-14.

decisions.choice: karama
decisions.reason: As 1:7 and chapter 12: "karama" is a gift of God's grace, here the ability for married or unmarried life; "zawadi" is an ordinary present.

decisions.choice: watu wote, kila mtu, yake: no gender span
decisions.reason: The Swahili words are already inclusive, and "wanaume" would mean males only, so the English gender spans have no Swahili counterpart.

source.text: Λέγω δὲ τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ·

records.literal_gloss: I say but to the unmarried and to the widows, good for them if they remain as also I;

en.L: But I say to the unmarried and to the widows: [it is] good for them if they remain as I also [am].
en.B: Now I say to the unmarried and to widows: it is a good thing for them if they stay as I am.
en.R: Here is what I say to people who are not married, and to widows: it is good for them to stay unmarried, just like me.

fr.L: Mais je dis aux non-mariés et aux veuves : [il est] bon pour eux de rester comme moi aussi.
fr.B: Je dis maintenant à ceux qui ne sont pas mariés et aux veuves : c’est une bonne chose pour eux de rester comme moi.
fr.R: Voici ce que je dis aux personnes qui ne sont pas mariées, et aux veuves : c’est bien pour elles de rester sans se marier, comme moi.

es.L: Pero digo a los no casados y a las viudas: bueno [es] para ellos si permanecen como también yo.
es.B: Ahora bien, a los no casados y a las viudas les digo que es bueno que se queden como yo.
es.R: Esto es lo que digo a quienes no están casados y a las viudas: es bueno que sigan sin casarse, como yo.

sw.L: Lakini nasema kwa wasio na ndoa na kwa wajane: [ni] vizuri kwao kama wakibaki kama mimi pia.
sw.B: Basi nawaambia wasio na ndoa na wajane: ni jambo jema kwao wakibaki kama nilivyo mimi.
sw.R: Hiki ndicho ninachowaambia watu wasio na ndoa, na wajane: ni vizuri wabaki bila kuoa au kuolewa, kama mimi.

decisions.choice: the unmarried: unmarried people in general, or perhaps widowers in particular
decisions.reason: ἀγάμοις is masculine plural, which can include women. Because it is paired with "widows", some take it to mean men whose wives have died. In verses 11 and 34 the same word is used of a separated wife and of an unmarried woman, so it is not limited to men.

decisions.choice: good if they remain as I am: staying unmarried is a good choice, not a requirement
decisions.reason: καλὸν ("good") echoes verse 1, but here Paul speaks for himself and at once allows marriage (verse 9). μείνωσιν means to stay as one is.

decisions.choice: stay as I am (B); stay unmarried, just like me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul's state was (verse 7, m1 there).

decisions.choice: les non-mariés (L); ceux qui ne sont pas mariés (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Célibataire" is usually heard as someone never married, but this word can include the widowed (m1), so French says plainly "not married", as the English "unmarried".

decisions.choice: los no casados (L, B); quienes no están casados (R)
decisions.reason: "Solteros" usually means people who have never married, but this word covers anyone without a spouse, perhaps the widowed (m1), so every level says "not married".

decisions.choice: wasio na ndoa
decisions.reason: "Wasiooa" would mean men only, while the meaning decision leaves open whether all unmarried people or widowers are meant; "wasio na ndoa" (those without a marriage) keeps that open.

source.text: εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἐγκρατεύονται, γαμησάτωσαν, κρεῖττον γάρ ἐστιν γαμῆσαι ἢ πυροῦσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: If but not they exercise self-control, let them marry, better for it is to marry than to burn.

en.L: But if they do not exercise self-control, let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn.
en.B: But if they are not keeping themselves under control, let them marry, for marrying is better than burning with desire.
en.R: But if they are not controlling their sexual desires, they should get married. Being married is better than burning with desire.

fr.L: Mais s’ils ne se maîtrisent pas, qu’ils se marient, car il vaut mieux se marier que brûler.
fr.B: Mais s’ils ne parviennent pas à se maîtriser, qu’ils se marient, car il vaut mieux se marier que brûler de désir.
fr.R: Mais s’ils n’arrivent pas à maîtriser leurs désirs sexuels, ils doivent se marier. Il vaut mieux être marié que brûler de désir.

es.L: Pero si no tienen dominio propio, que se casen, porque mejor es casarse que quemarse.
es.B: Pero si no se están controlando, que se casen, porque es mejor casarse que quemarse de deseo.
es.R: Pero si no están controlando sus deseos sexuales, deben casarse. Estar casado es mejor que quemarse de deseo.

sw.L: Lakini kama hawajizuii, na wafunge ndoa; kwa maana ni afadhali kufunga ndoa kuliko kuwaka.
sw.B: Lakini kama hawajizuii, na wafunge ndoa, kwa maana ni afadhali kufunga ndoa kuliko kuwaka kwa tamaa.
sw.R: Lakini kama hawazizuii tamaa zao za ngono, wafunge ndoa. Ni afadhali kuwa katika ndoa kuliko kuwaka kwa tamaa.

decisions.choice: do not exercise self-control: they are in fact not managing to control their desires
decisions.reason: ἐγκρατεύονται is a plain present: Paul describes people who are actually struggling, not a mere possibility. It is the verb related to "lack of self-control" in verse 5.

decisions.choice: burn: burn with sexual desire
decisions.reason: πυροῦσθαι was used for being inflamed with passion as well as for literal burning (compare 2 Corinthians 11:29). The contrast with marrying points to desire; nothing in the passage speaks of judgment.

decisions.choice: burning with desire
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "with desire" so the figure is not taken as judgment (m2); Literal keeps "burn".

decisions.choice: kufunga ndoa
decisions.reason: Swahili says "kuoa" of a man and "kuolewa" of a woman; where Paul speaks of both, as here, the neutral "kufunga ndoa" (to marry, to make a marriage) is used. Where he speaks of a man or a woman alone, "kuoa" or "kuolewa".

source.text: Τοῖς δὲ γεγαμηκόσιν παραγγέλλω, οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλὰ ὁ κύριος, γυναῖκα ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς μὴ χωρισθῆναι ἐὰν δὲ καὶ χωρισθῇ, μενέτω ἄγαμος ἢ τῷ ἀνδρὶ καταλλαγήτω καὶ ἄνδρα γυναῖκα μὴ ἀφιέναι.

records.literal_gloss: To the but having married I command, not I but the Lord, a wife from a husband not to be separated \v 11 if but also she be separated, let her remain unmarried or to the husband let her be reconciled and a husband a wife not to leave.

en.L: But to the married I command, not I but the Lord, [that a] wife is not to separate from [her] husband \v 11 (but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to [her] husband), and [that a] husband is not to leave [his] wife.
en.B: To those who are married I give a charge, and it is the Lord's, not mine: a wife is not to leave her husband. \v 11 If she does separate, she should either stay unmarried or be reconciled with him. And a husband is not to divorce his wife.
en.R: To married people I give a command. It does not come from me but from the Lord: a wife must not leave her husband. \v 11 But if she does leave him, she must not marry anyone else. Or else she should make peace with her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.

fr.L: Mais à ceux qui sont mariés j’ordonne, non pas moi mais le Seigneur, que la femme ne se sépare pas de [son] mari \v 11 (mais si elle s’en sépare, qu’elle reste non mariée ou qu’elle se réconcilie avec [son] mari), et que le mari ne quitte pas [sa] femme.
fr.B: À ceux qui sont mariés, je donne cet ordre, qui vient du Seigneur et non de moi : la femme ne doit pas quitter son mari. \v 11 Si elle s’en sépare, qu’elle reste sans se remarier ou qu’elle se réconcilie avec lui. Et le mari ne doit pas divorcer de sa femme.
fr.R: Aux personnes mariées, je donne un ordre. Il ne vient pas de moi, mais du Seigneur : une femme ne doit pas quitter son mari. \v 11 Mais si elle le quitte, elle ne doit pas épouser un autre homme. Ou bien, elle doit faire la paix avec son mari. Et un mari ne doit pas divorcer de sa femme.

es.L: Y a los que se han casado les ordeno, no yo, sino el Señor: que [la] mujer no se separe de [su] marido \v 11 (pero si se separa, que permanezca sin casarse o que se reconcilie con el marido), y que [el] marido no deje a [su] mujer.
es.B: A los que están casados les doy un mandato, que no es mío sino del Señor: que la mujer no se separe de su marido. \v 11 Si llega a separarse, que se quede sin casarse o que se reconcilie con él. Y que el marido no se divorcie de su mujer.
es.R: A los casados les doy un mandato. No viene de mí, sino del Señor: la esposa no debe dejar a su esposo. \v 11 Pero si lo deja, no debe casarse con otro. O, si no, debe hacer las paces con su esposo. Y el esposo no debe divorciarse de su esposa.

sw.L: Lakini kwa waliooana naagiza, si mimi bali Bwana, mke asitengane na mume \v 11 (lakini akitengana, na abaki bila kuolewa au apatane na mume [wake]), na mume asimwache mke.
sw.B: Kwa wale walio katika ndoa natoa agizo, nalo si langu bali ni la Bwana: mke asimwache mumewe. \v 11 Na ikiwa ameachana naye, abaki bila kuolewa au apatane na mumewe. Na mume asimtaliki mkewe.
sw.R: Kwa watu walio katika ndoa natoa amri. Haitoki kwangu bali kwa Bwana: mke asimwache mumewe. \v 11 Lakini kama amemwacha, asiolewe na mwanamume mwingine. Au sivyo apatane na mumewe. Na mume asimtaliki mkewe.

decisions.choice: not I but the Lord: Jesus' own teaching on divorce
decisions.reason: Jesus forbade divorce and remarriage (Mark 10:2-12; Matthew 5:31-32; 19:3-9; Luke 16:18). Paul passes on that teaching as a command of the Lord. In verse 12 and verse 25 he marks where he has no word of the Lord and speaks for himself.

decisions.choice: separate, leave: end the marriage; in practice, divorce
alternatives: a separation that leaves the marriage in place
decisions.reason: χωρισθῆναι and ἀφιέναι were both used for divorce in the Greek of the time. Under Roman law either spouse could end a marriage simply by leaving; no court was needed. That is why the wife who separates is called ἄγαμος, "unmarried". The two verbs vary the wording more than the meaning, though the wife is said to leave and the husband to send away.

decisions.choice: if she does separate ... : an aside within the Lord's command
alternatives: a separate instruction after the command
decisions.reason: The words in verse 11 interrupt the sentence, which then goes on with the husband's duty. Printed editions mark them off as a parenthesis. Paul allows for what may already have happened while keeping the command: such a wife is not free to marry someone else.

decisions.choice: leave (B, R wife); divorce (B, R husband)
decisions.reason: Both mean ending the marriage (m2); Balanced and Readable use the words a modern reader would use. Literal keeps "separate" and "leave".

decisions.choice: must not marry anyone else; make peace with her husband
decisions.reason: Readable says what staying unmarried means here and uses everyday words for reconciliation.

decisions.choice: separarse, dejar (L); separarse, divorciarse de (B, R)
decisions.reason: Both verbs mean ending the marriage (m2). Literal keeps the two Greek pictures, "separarse" and "dejar"; Balanced and Readable say "divorciarse de" for the husband, as in Mark 10, and keep "separarse" or "dejar" for the wife, as the English does. "Repudiar" is an older legal word few readers use.

decisions.choice: asimwache (the wife); asimtaliki (the husband)
decisions.reason: As the English: the wife "leaves", the husband "divorces". In Swahili usage "kutaliki" is said of a husband, so it is not used of the wife; the meaning (ending the marriage) is the same for both.

source.text: Τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς λέγω ἐγώ, οὐχ ὁ κύριος· εἴ τις ἀδελφὸς γυναῖκα ἔχει ἄπιστον, καὶ αὕτη συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετ’ αὐτοῦ, μὴ ἀφιέτω αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: To the but rest say I, not the Lord: if any brother a wife has unbelieving, and she consents to live with him, let him not leave her;

en.L: But to the rest I say, I, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she consents to live with him, let him not leave her.
en.B: To everyone else I say this myself; it is not a word from the Lord. Suppose a brother has a wife who does not believe, and she is content to go on living with him: he must not divorce her.
en.R: To the rest of you I say this. It is my own word, not a command from the Lord. If a man who is a believer has a wife who does not believe, and she is happy to stay married to him, he must not divorce her.

fr.L: Mais aux autres je dis, moi, non le Seigneur : si quelque frère a une femme incroyante, et qu’elle consent à habiter avec lui, qu’il ne la quitte pas.
fr.B: Aux autres, c’est moi qui le dis, ce n’est pas une parole du Seigneur : si un frère a une femme qui ne croit pas, et qu’elle est d’accord pour continuer à vivre avec lui, il ne doit pas divorcer d’elle.
fr.R: Aux autres, je dis ceci. C’est ma parole à moi, pas un ordre du Seigneur. Si un homme croyant a une femme qui ne croit pas, et qu’elle est heureuse de rester mariée avec lui, il ne doit pas divorcer d’elle.

es.L: Pero a los demás les digo yo, no el Señor: si algún hermano tiene una mujer no creyente, y ella consiente en vivir con él, que no la deje.
es.B: A todos los demás les digo esto yo mismo; no es una palabra del Señor. Supongamos que un hermano tiene una mujer que no es creyente, y ella está conforme con seguir viviendo con él: él no debe divorciarse de ella.
es.R: A los demás {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto. Es mi propia palabra, no un mandato del Señor. Si un hombre creyente tiene una esposa que no cree, y ella está contenta de seguir casada con él, él no debe divorciarse de ella.

sw.L: Lakini kwa wengine nasema mimi, si Bwana: kama ndugu yeyote ana mke asiyeamini, naye anakubali kuishi pamoja naye, asimwache.
sw.B: Kwa wengine wote nasema mimi mwenyewe; si neno kutoka kwa Bwana. Tuseme ndugu ana mke asiyeamini, na mke huyo yuko radhi kuendelea kuishi naye: asimtaliki.
sw.R: Kwa ninyi wengine nasema hivi. Ni neno langu mwenyewe, si amri kutoka kwa Bwana. Ikiwa mwanamume aliye mwamini ana mke asiyeamini, na mke huyo anafurahi kuendelea kuishi naye katika ndoa, asimtaliki.

decisions.choice: the rest: believers married to unbelievers; I, not the Lord: Jesus left no saying on this case
alternatives: Paul's word carries less authority than the Lord's
decisions.reason: λοιποῖς are those not covered by verses 10-11: couples where only one partner has come to faith. Jesus spoke to married people within God's people; he gave no ruling on this new situation. Paul still speaks with an apostle's authority (verses 17 and 40; 14:37).

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, here a man
decisions.reason: ἀδελφὸς is Paul's usual word for a member of the church. Here it means one particular kind of person, a believing husband; verse 15 names "the brother or the sister".

decisions.choice: unbelieving: not a believer in Christ
decisions.reason: ἄπιστον is used throughout this letter of people outside the church (6:6; 10:27; 14:22-24). It says nothing about the wife's loyalty to her husband.

decisions.choice: a man who is a believer
decisions.reason: Readable says who "brother" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: divorce
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the verb means ending the marriage. Literal keeps "leave".

decisions.choice: algún hermano, no setting
decisions.reason: Here the brother is a man with a wife (m2), so Spanish has only "hermano", as the English has no gender span.

source.text: καὶ γυνὴ εἴ τις ἔχει ἄνδρα ἄπιστον, καὶ οὗτος συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετ’ αὐτῆς, μὴ ἀφιέτω τὸν ἄνδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And a wife if any has a husband unbelieving, and he consents to live with her, let her not leave the husband.

en.L: And if any wife has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to live with her, let her not leave the husband.
en.B: And if a woman has a husband who does not believe, and he is content to go on living with her, she must not divorce him.
en.R: And if a woman who is a believer has a husband who does not believe, and he is happy to stay married to her, she must not divorce him.

fr.L: Et si quelque femme a un mari incroyant, et qu’il consent à habiter avec elle, qu’elle ne quitte pas le mari.
fr.B: Et si une femme a un mari qui ne croit pas, et qu’il est d’accord pour continuer à vivre avec elle, elle ne doit pas divorcer de lui.
fr.R: Et si une femme croyante a un mari qui ne croit pas, et qu’il est heureux de rester marié avec elle, elle ne doit pas divorcer de lui.

es.L: Y si alguna mujer tiene un marido no creyente, y él consiente en vivir con ella, que no deje al marido.
es.B: Y si una mujer tiene un marido que no es creyente, y él está conforme con seguir viviendo con ella, ella no debe divorciarse de él.
es.R: Y si una mujer creyente tiene un esposo que no cree, y él está contento de seguir casado con ella, ella no debe divorciarse de él.

sw.L: Na mke yeyote akiwa na mume asiyeamini, naye anakubali kuishi pamoja naye, asimwache mume.
sw.B: Na ikiwa mwanamke ana mume asiyeamini, na mume huyo yuko radhi kuendelea kuishi naye, asimwache.
sw.R: Na ikiwa mwanamke aliye mwamini ana mume asiyeamini, na mume huyo anafurahi kuendelea kuishi naye katika ndoa, asimwache.

decisions.choice: let her not leave: a wife could end a marriage too
decisions.reason: Under Roman law a wife, as well as a husband, could divorce. Here Paul uses for the wife the same verb, ἀφιέτω, that he used for the husband in verse 12, and gives her the same rule.

decisions.choice: a wife: a believing wife, matching the "brother" of verse 12
decisions.reason: The parallel with verse 12 shows that she is a believer, as verse 14 confirms.

decisions.choice: divorce him
decisions.reason: As in verse 12; Literal keeps "leave" and repeats "the husband" as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: asimwache
decisions.reason: The English says "divorce him"; Swahili "kutaliki" is said of a husband, so the wife's ending of the marriage is "kumwacha" (leave him), which the meaning decision's point (a wife could end a marriage too) still carries.

source.text: ἡγίασται γὰρ ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἄπιστος ἐν τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἡγίασται ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄπιστος ἐν τῷ ἀδελφῷ· ἐπεὶ ἄρα τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν ἀκάθαρτά ἐστιν, νῦν δὲ ἅγιά ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Has been made holy for the husband the unbelieving in the wife, and has been made holy the wife the unbelieving in the brother; since then the children of you unclean are, but now holy they are.

en.L: For the unbelieving husband has been made holy in the wife, and the unbelieving wife has been made holy in the brother; since otherwise your children are unclean, but now they are holy.
en.B: For through his wife the husband who does not believe has been made holy, and through the brother she is married to, the wife who does not believe has been made holy. If it were not so, your children would be unclean; in fact, they are holy.
en.R: A husband who does not believe is made holy because of his wife, who believes. And a wife who does not believe is made holy because of her husband, who believes. If this were not true, your children would be unclean, not set apart for God. But they are holy.

fr.L: Car le mari incroyant a été sanctifié dans la femme, et la femme incroyante a été sanctifiée dans le frère ; autrement vos enfants sont impurs, mais maintenant ils sont saints.
fr.B: Car le mari qui ne croit pas a été rendu saint par sa femme, et la femme qui ne croit pas a été rendue sainte par le frère qu’elle a épousé. S’il n’en était pas ainsi, vos enfants seraient impurs ; en réalité, ils sont saints.
fr.R: Un mari qui ne croit pas est rendu saint grâce à sa femme, qui croit. Et une femme qui ne croit pas est rendue sainte grâce à son mari, qui croit. Si ce n’était pas vrai, vos enfants seraient impurs, ils ne seraient pas mis à part pour Dieu. Mais ils sont saints.

es.L: Porque el marido no creyente ha sido santificado en la mujer, y la mujer no creyente ha sido santificada en el hermano; pues de otro modo {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos serían impuros, pero ahora son santos.
es.B: Porque el marido no creyente ha sido santificado por medio de su mujer, y la mujer no creyente ha sido santificada por medio del hermano con quien está casada. Si no fuera así, {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos serían impuros; pero, de hecho, son santos.
es.R: Un esposo que no cree queda santificado gracias a su esposa, que sí cree. Y una esposa que no cree queda santificada gracias a su esposo, que sí cree. Si esto no fuera así, {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos serían impuros, no apartados para Dios. Pero son santos.

sw.L: Kwa maana mume asiyeamini ametakaswa katika mke, na mke asiyeamini ametakaswa katika ndugu; kwa kuwa vinginevyo watoto wenu ni najisi, lakini sasa ni watakatifu.
sw.B: Kwa maana mume asiyeamini ametakaswa kupitia mkewe, na mke asiyeamini ametakaswa kupitia ndugu aliyemwoa. Kama sivyo, watoto wenu wangekuwa najisi; lakini kwa kweli wao ni watakatifu.
sw.R: Mume asiyeamini anafanywa mtakatifu kwa sababu ya mkewe, aliye mwamini. Na mke asiyeamini anafanywa mtakatifu kwa sababu ya mumewe, aliye mwamini. Kama hili lisingekuwa kweli, watoto wenu wangekuwa najisi, wasiotengwa kwa ajili ya Mungu. Lakini wao ni watakatifu.

decisions.choice: made holy: set apart and brought within the reach of God's holiness through the marriage, but not saved
alternatives: saved, or made a Christian, through the believing spouse
the marriage is acceptable to God
decisions.reason: ἡγίασται is the verb used in 1:2 and 6:11 of believers. But verse 16 shows that the unbelieving partner is not yet saved. Some in Corinth may have feared that union with an unbeliever made the believer unclean, as union with a prostitute did (6:15-17). Paul answers that the influence runs the other way: holiness reaches from the believer to the spouse and the home. How far this goes is not spelled out.

decisions.choice: in the wife, in the brother: by being joined to the believing spouse
decisions.reason: ἐν here gives the sphere or means: through the marriage bond with a believer.

decisions.choice: otherwise your children would be unclean: an argument from what the church already accepted
decisions.reason: ἐπεὶ ἄρα means "since otherwise". Paul assumes his readers already count the children of a believing parent as belonging to God; the same must then be true of the unbelieving spouse. "Unclean" and "holy" are the Old Testament terms for what may or may not come near God.

decisions.choice: through (B); because of (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "in" means by virtue of the union (m2); Literal keeps "in".

decisions.choice: the brother she is married to (B); her husband, who believes (R); not set apart for God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced makes clear that "the brother" is the believing husband; Readable says so plainly and says what "unclean" means.

decisions.choice: sanctifié (L); rendu saint (B, R), as in 6:11
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 6:11 gets the same French, so that the reader can see the link; "rendu saint" also keeps the word "saints" used of the children at the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: serían impuros
decisions.reason: The Greek says "are unclean" after "since otherwise", an unreal condition. Spanish needs the conditional "serían" there, even at Literal, to be grammatical.

decisions.choice: najisi
decisions.reason: "Najisi" is unclean in the religious sense, set against "watakatifu" (holy); "wachafu" would suggest dirt.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεται, χωριζέσθω· οὐ δεδούλωται ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις, ἐν δὲ εἰρήνῃ κέκληκεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: If but the unbelieving separates, let him separate; not has been enslaved the brother or the sister in the such [cases], in but peace has called us the God.

en.L: But if the unbeliever separates, let [that one] separate; the brother or the sister has not been enslaved in such [cases]; but God has called us in peace.
en.B: But if the one who does not believe chooses to separate, let the separation happen. A brother or a sister is not bound in circumstances like these. It is in peace that God has called us.
en.R: But if the husband or wife who does not believe wants to leave, let it happen. In that case the believing husband or wife is not tied to the marriage. God called us so that we would live at peace.

fr.L: Mais si l’incroyant se sépare, qu’il se sépare ; le frère ou la sœur n’est pas asservi dans de tels [cas] ; mais Dieu nous a appelés dans la paix.
fr.B: Mais si celui qui ne croit pas choisit de se séparer, qu’il le fasse. Dans ces cas-là, le frère ou la sœur n’est pas lié. C’est dans la paix que Dieu nous a appelés.
fr.R: Mais si le mari ou la femme qui ne croit pas veut partir, acceptez son départ. Dans ce cas, le mari ou la femme qui croit n’est plus attaché à ce mariage. Dieu nous a appelés pour que nous vivions en paix.

es.L: Pero si el no creyente se separa, que se separe; el hermano o la hermana no ha sido esclavizado en [casos] semejantes; pero Dios nos ha llamado en paz.
es.B: Pero si el que no es creyente decide separarse, que se separe. En casos como estos, el hermano o la hermana no está atado. Es en paz como Dios nos ha llamado.
es.R: Pero si el esposo o la esposa que no cree quiere irse, que se vaya. En ese caso, el esposo o la esposa que cree no está atado al matrimonio. Dios nos llamó para que vivamos en paz.

sw.L: Lakini kama asiyeamini anatengana, na atengane; ndugu wa kiume au ndugu wa kike hajafanywa mtumwa katika [mambo] kama hayo; lakini Mungu ametuita katika amani.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa yule asiyeamini anaamua kutengana, waache watengane. Ndugu wa kiume au wa kike hafungwi katika hali kama hizo. Mungu ametuita katika amani.
sw.R: Lakini ikiwa mume au mke asiyeamini anataka kuondoka, mwache aondoke. Katika hali hiyo, mume au mke aliye mwamini hafungwi na ndoa hiyo. Mungu alituita ili tuishi kwa amani.

decisions.choice: separates: chooses to end the marriage; let it happen
decisions.reason: χωρίζεται is the same verb as in verses 10-11, here of the unbelieving partner's own choice. χωριζέσθω tells the believer not to resist it.

decisions.choice: not bound: not obliged to hold the marriage together
alternatives: not enslaved to the unbeliever's wishes
decisions.reason: δεδούλωται means "has been enslaved", a strong word. The believer is not bound to keep a marriage the other has ended. Whether this also leaves the believer free to marry again is not stated; the text does not repeat the "stay unmarried" of verse 11, which some take as permission, while others hold that verse 39 still applies.

decisions.choice: God has called us in peace: a reason for letting the unbeliever go, rather than holding on at all costs
alternatives: a reason to keep the marriage if at all possible, leading into verse 16
decisions.reason: δὲ can mark a contrast or carry the thought on. Following "not bound", peace most naturally explains why the believer need not fight the separation. Others connect it with verse 16 as a call to keep the peace in the marriage.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "us"
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts read "you" instead of "us". The two words differed by one letter and sounded alike, so copyists often confused them. The meaning is little changed. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: has not been enslaved (L); is not bound (B); is not tied to the marriage (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the strong verb; Balanced and Readable give its sense here (m2).

decisions.choice: le frère ou la sœur, with no setting
decisions.reason: The Greek itself names both the brother and the sister, so French says both and needs no gender span. The generic "l’incroyant" and "celui qui ne croit pas" cover a husband or a wife.

decisions.choice: no ha sido esclavizado (L); no está atado (B); no está atado al matrimonio (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the slave picture of the Greek verb; Balanced and Readable say "atado", tied, as the English says "bound". The masculine participle agrees with "el hermano o la hermana" together, as Spanish does for a man and a woman named side by side.

decisions.choice: ndugu wa kiume au ndugu wa kike (L); ndugu wa kiume au wa kike (B)
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" alone covers both, but Paul names the brother and the sister separately, so Swahili spells out both.

source.text: τί γὰρ οἶδας, γύναι, εἰ τὸν ἄνδρα σώσεις;

records.literal_gloss: What for do you know, wife, whether the husband you will save?

en.L: For how do you know, wife, if you will save the husband?
en.B: How can you tell, wife, whether you will save your husband?
en.R: Wife, how do you know whether your husband will be saved through you?

fr.L: Car que sais-tu, femme, si tu sauveras le mari ?
fr.B: Comment peux-tu savoir, femme, si tu sauveras ton mari ?
fr.R: Toi, la femme, comment sais-tu si ton mari sera sauvé grâce à toi ?

es.L: Pues ¿qué sabes, mujer, si salvarás al marido?
es.B: ¿Cómo puedes saber, mujer, si salvarás a tu marido?
es.R: Esposa, ¿cómo sabes si tu esposo se salvará por medio de ti?

sw.L: Kwa maana unajuaje, mke, kama utamwokoa mume?
sw.B: Wewe mke, unawezaje kujua kama utamwokoa mumeo?
sw.R: Wewe mke, unajuaje kama mumeo ataokolewa kupitia kwako?

decisions.choice: how do you know whether ...: you cannot be sure that staying will lead to your spouse's salvation
alternatives: perhaps you will save your spouse, so try to keep the marriage
decisions.reason: γὰρ links the question to verse 15. Read that way, Paul tells the believer not to hold on to an unwilling partner in the hope of winning them, since no one can know that. The question can also be heard hopefully, "who knows, you may save him", as a reason to stay (verses 12-13). The Greek allows both.

decisions.choice: save: bring the spouse to salvation, through faith in Christ
decisions.reason: σώσεις means to save in the full sense (1:18, 21). Paul speaks of the believer being the means of it (9:22); being made holy (verse 14) is not the same as being saved.

decisions.choice: your husband will be saved through you
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the wife is the means of his salvation, not its source.

decisions.choice: tu (every level)
decisions.reason: Paul turns to one wife, and then to one husband, with a singular verb, so French says "tu", as the style guide sets for one addressee.

decisions.choice: sabes (tú), no plural_you setting
decisions.reason: Paul turns to one wife and then to one husband in the singular, so Spanish uses "tú", which needs no ustedes/vosotros setting.

source.text: ἢ τί οἶδας, ἄνερ, εἰ τὴν γυναῖκα σώσεις;

records.literal_gloss: Or what do you know, husband, whether the wife you will save?

en.L: Or how do you know, husband, if you will save the wife?
en.B: Or how can you tell, husband, whether you will save your wife?
en.R: And husband, how do you know whether your wife will be saved through you?

fr.L: Ou que sais-tu, mari, si tu sauveras la femme ?
fr.B: Ou comment peux-tu savoir, mari, si tu sauveras ta femme ?
fr.R: Et toi, le mari, comment sais-tu si ta femme sera sauvée grâce à toi ?

es.L: ¿O qué sabes, marido, si salvarás a la mujer?
es.B: ¿O cómo puedes saber, marido, si salvarás a tu mujer?
es.R: Y tú, esposo, ¿cómo sabes si tu esposa se salvará por medio de ti?

sw.L: Au unajuaje, mume, kama utamwokoa mke?
sw.B: Au wewe mume, unawezaje kujua kama utamwokoa mkeo?
sw.R: Na wewe mume, unajuaje kama mkeo ataokolewa kupitia kwako?

decisions.choice: the same question, put to the husband
decisions.reason: Paul again speaks to husband and wife in matching words. The question carries the same meaning as the one before it (16a, m1).

decisions.choice: your wife will be saved through you
decisions.reason: As in 16a.

source.text: Εἰ μὴ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ἐμέρισεν ὁ κύριος, ἕκαστον ὡς κέκληκεν ὁ θεός, οὕτως περιπατείτω· καὶ οὕτως ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις πάσαις διατάσσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: Except to each as has assigned the Lord, each as has called the God, so let him walk; and so in the churches all I direct.

en.L: Only, as the Lord has assigned to each, as God has called each, so let each walk. And so I direct in all the churches.
en.B: Whatever the case, each of you should lead the life the Lord has given you, the life you had when God called you. I give this same direction in every church.
en.R: But each of you should keep living the life the Lord has given you. Stay in the situation you were in when God called you. This is what I teach in all the churches.

fr.L: Seulement, chacun, comme le Seigneur [lui] a donné sa part, chacun, comme Dieu [l’]a appelé, qu’il marche ainsi. Et c’est ce que je prescris dans toutes les églises.
fr.B: Quoi qu’il en soit, que chacun de vous mène la vie que le Seigneur lui a donnée, la vie qu’il avait quand Dieu l’a appelé. C’est la même règle que je donne dans toutes les églises.
fr.R: Mais chacun de vous doit continuer à vivre la vie que le Seigneur lui a donnée. Restez dans la situation où vous étiez quand Dieu vous a appelés. C’est ce que j’enseigne dans toutes les églises.

es.L: Solamente, como el Señor ha repartido a cada uno, como Dios ha llamado a cada uno, así ande [cada uno]. Y así lo dispongo en todas las iglesias.
es.B: Sea como sea, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe llevar la vida que el Señor le ha dado, la vida que tenía cuando Dios lo llamó. Esto mismo es lo que dispongo en todas las iglesias.
es.R: Pero cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe seguir viviendo la vida que el Señor le ha dado. Que cada uno siga en la situación en que estaba cuando Dios lo llamó. Esto es lo que enseño en todas las iglesias.

sw.L: Ila tu, kama Bwana alivyomgawia kila mmoja, kama Mungu alivyomwita kila mmoja, hivyo na aenende. Na hivyo ndivyo ninavyoagiza katika makanisa yote.
sw.B: Iwe vyovyote vile, kila mmoja wenu na aishi maisha ambayo Bwana amempa, maisha aliyokuwa nayo Mungu alipomwita. Ninatoa agizo hili hili katika makanisa yote.
sw.R: Lakini kila mmoja wenu aendelee kuishi maisha ambayo Bwana amempa. Kila mmoja abaki katika hali aliyokuwa nayo Mungu alipomwita. Hivi ndivyo ninavyofundisha katika makanisa yote.

decisions.choice: only, in any case: Paul turns from the exception back to the rule
decisions.reason: Εἰ μὴ, normally "except", here means "only" or "in any case". Having allowed that a marriage may end (verse 15), Paul states the general rule that governs the rest of the chapter: stay in the situation you were in when called. He says it three times (verses 17, 20 and 24).

decisions.choice: assigned, called: the place in life the Lord gave, and God's call to faith that came there
decisions.reason: ἐμέρισεν means to give each a portion or share. κέκληκεν is God's call that brought them to faith (1:9, 26). The two lines say the same thing from two sides: the situation the Lord gave, and the call that came to them in it.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: περιπατείτω is Paul's usual word for a way of life (3:3; Colossians 1:10).

decisions.choice: I direct this in all the churches: the rule is not special to Corinth
decisions.reason: διατάσσομαι means to give orders or arrange. Paul often reminds the Corinthians that what he asks of them he asks of every church (4:17; 11:16; 14:33).

decisions.choice: lead the life (B); keep living the life (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" in this sense is not everyday English; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: the life you had when God called you (B); the situation you were in when God called you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "as God has called" refers to (m2).

decisions.choice: qu’il marche (L), mener sa vie (B, R); les églises, lowercase
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the image of walking for one's way of life, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m3). The churches are many local congregations, so the lowercase of the style guide applies.

decisions.choice: ande
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of walking for the way one lives (m3), as Spanish "andar" is used in Romans 14:15; Balanced and Readable say "llevar la vida" and "seguir viviendo".

decisions.choice: aenende
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of walking ("kuenenda") for the way one lives; Balanced and Readable say "kuishi".

source.text: περιτετμημένος τις ἐκλήθη;

records.literal_gloss: Having been circumcised anyone was called?

en.L: Was anyone called having been circumcised?
en.B: Was someone already circumcised when he was called?
en.R: Was a man already circumcised when God called him?

fr.L: Quelqu’un a-t-il été appelé étant circoncis ?
fr.B: Quelqu’un était-il déjà circoncis quand il a été appelé ?
fr.R: Un homme était-il déjà circoncis quand Dieu l’a appelé ?

es.L: ¿Fue llamado alguno estando circuncidado?
es.B: ¿Ya estaba circuncidado alguien cuando fue llamado?
es.R: ¿Ya estaba circuncidado un hombre cuando Dios lo llamó?

sw.L: Je, mtu yeyote aliitwa akiwa ametahiriwa?
sw.B: Je, mtu alikuwa ameshatahiriwa alipoitwa?
sw.R: Je, mwanamume alikuwa ameshatahiriwa Mungu alipomwita?

decisions.choice: circumcised: a Jewish man, marked by circumcision
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 17:10-14). In a mixed church it marked out the Jewish men from the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: was called: was called by God to faith
decisions.reason: ἐκλήθη is passive with God as the one who calls (verse 17), as throughout this passage.

decisions.choice: when God called him
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who called.

source.text: μὴ ἐπισπάσθω· ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ κέκληταί τις;

records.literal_gloss: Let him not draw over; in uncircumcision has been called anyone?

en.L: Let him not undo [his circumcision]. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision?
en.B: He must not try to reverse it. Was someone uncircumcised when he was called?
en.R: Then he should not try to undo it. Was a man not circumcised when God called him?

fr.L: Qu’il ne défasse pas [sa circoncision]. Quelqu’un a-t-il été appelé dans l’incirconcision ?
fr.B: Il ne doit pas chercher à en effacer la marque. Quelqu’un était-il incirconcis quand il a été appelé ?
fr.R: Alors il ne doit pas essayer de la faire disparaître. Un homme n’était-il pas circoncis quand Dieu l’a appelé ?

es.L: Que no se cubra [la circuncisión]. ¿Ha sido llamado alguno en incircuncisión?
es.B: Que no intente deshacerla. ¿No estaba circuncidado alguien cuando fue llamado?
es.R: Entonces no debe intentar deshacerla. ¿No estaba circuncidado un hombre cuando Dios lo llamó?

sw.L: Asiiondoe [tohara yake]. Je, mtu yeyote ameitwa katika hali ya kutotahiriwa?
sw.B: Asijaribu kuiondoa. Je, mtu alikuwa hajatahiriwa alipoitwa?
sw.R: Basi asijaribu kuiondoa. Je, mwanamume alikuwa hajatahiriwa Mungu alipomwita?

decisions.choice: undo: have the marks of circumcision hidden by surgery
decisions.reason: ἐπισπάσθω means "draw over". Some Jewish men in the Greek world had an operation to hide their circumcision, to avoid mockery in the gymnasium or to fit in (1 Maccabees 1:15). Paul tells Jewish believers not to do so.

decisions.choice: in uncircumcision: as a Gentile
decisions.reason: ἀκροβυστίᾳ, uncircumcision, stands for the state of a Gentile man.

decisions.choice: try to reverse it (B); try to undo it (R)
decisions.reason: The literal "draw over" means nothing to a modern reader (m1).

decisions.choice: se cubra [la circuncisión] (L); deshacerla (B, R); en incircuncisión (L); no estaba circuncidado (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to draw over, hiding the mark of circumcision (m1); Literal keeps that picture and Balanced and Readable say "undo it". Literal keeps the noun "incircuncisión", as Galatians 5:6 does; the other levels say "not circumcised", which is plainer than "incircunciso".

decisions.choice: asiiondoe [tohara yake] (L); asijaribu kuiondoa (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kuiondoa" (remove it, undo it) says what the operation set out to do, as the English "undo, reverse"; the meaning decision explains the practice.

source.text: μὴ περιτεμνέσθω.

records.literal_gloss: Let him not be circumcised.

en.L: Let him not be circumcised.
en.B: He must not get circumcised.
en.R: Then he should not get circumcised.

fr.L: Qu’il ne se fasse pas circoncire.
fr.B: Il ne doit pas se faire circoncire.
fr.R: Alors il ne doit pas se faire circoncire.

es.L: Que no se circuncide.
es.B: Que no se haga circuncidar.
es.R: Entonces no debe circuncidarse.

sw.L: Asitahiriwe.
sw.B: Asikubali kutahiriwa.
sw.R: Basi asitahiriwe.

decisions.choice: not be circumcised: a Gentile believer need not become a Jew
decisions.reason: Some taught that Gentile believers must be circumcised (Acts 15:1, 5; Galatians 5:2-6). Paul rejects this here as in his other letters.

source.text: ἡ περιτομὴ οὐδέν ἐστιν, καὶ ἡ ἀκροβυστία οὐδέν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ τήρησις ἐντολῶν θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The circumcision nothing is, and the uncircumcision nothing is, but keeping of commandments of God.

en.L: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but [what matters is the] keeping of [the] commandments of God.
en.B: Being circumcised means nothing, and not being circumcised means nothing. What matters is obeying the commandments of God.
en.R: It does not matter whether a man is circumcised or not. What matters is doing what God commands.

fr.L: La circoncision n’est rien, et l’incirconcision n’est rien, mais [ce qui compte, c’est] l’observation des commandements de Dieu.
fr.B: Être circoncis ne compte pour rien, et ne pas l’être ne compte pour rien. Ce qui compte, c’est d’obéir aux commandements de Dieu.
fr.R: Qu’un homme soit circoncis ou non, cela n’a pas d’importance. Ce qui compte, c’est de faire ce que Dieu commande.

es.L: La circuncisión nada es, y la incircuncisión nada es, sino [lo que importa es] el cumplimiento de [los] mandamientos de Dios.
es.B: Estar circuncidado no significa nada, y no estarlo tampoco significa nada. Lo que importa es obedecer los mandamientos de Dios.
es.R: No importa si un hombre está circuncidado o no. Lo que importa es hacer lo que Dios manda.

sw.L: Tohara si kitu, na kutotahiriwa si kitu, bali [kilicho muhimu ni] kuzishika amri za Mungu.
sw.B: Kutahiriwa si kitu, na kutotahiriwa si kitu. Kilicho muhimu ni kuzitii amri za Mungu.
sw.R: Haijalishi kama mwanamume ametahiriwa au la. Kilicho muhimu ni kufanya yale ambayo Mungu ameamuru.

decisions.choice: keeping God's commandments: doing God's will, which is what counts, not one's birth or mark
decisions.reason: The saying is startling, because circumcision was itself one of God's commandments (Genesis 17:10). Paul means God's will as now made known in Christ. Galatians 5:6 and 6:15 make the same contrast with "faith working through love" and "a new creation".

decisions.choice: but ...: the verb is left out
decisions.reason: After ἀλλὰ the Greek simply names "keeping of the commandments of God"; the meaning is that this, unlike circumcision, is what counts.

decisions.choice: what matters
decisions.reason: English needs a verb here (m2). Literal puts it in brackets.

decisions.choice: tohara, kutotahiriwa (L); kutahiriwa, kutotahiriwa (B)
decisions.reason: As Colossians 2-3 and Galatians: "tohara" and "kutotahiriwa", the forms Swahili uses for the pair.

source.text: ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ κλήσει ᾗ ἐκλήθη ἐν ταύτῃ μενέτω.

records.literal_gloss: Each in the calling in which he was called, in this let him remain.

en.L: Each one, in the calling in which {{gender:they were|he was}} called, in it let {{gender:them|him}} remain.
en.B: Each of you should go on in the place in life where God's call found you.
en.R: Each of you should stay as you were when God called you.

fr.L: Chacun, dans l’appel par lequel il a été appelé, qu’il y demeure.
fr.B: Que chacun de vous continue de vivre dans la situation où l’appel de Dieu l’a trouvé.
fr.R: Chacun de vous doit rester tel qu’il était quand Dieu l’a appelé.

es.L: Cada uno, en el llamamiento en que fue llamado, en él permanezca.
es.B: Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe seguir en el lugar de la vida en que lo encontró el llamamiento de Dios.
es.R: Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe quedarse como estaba cuando Dios lo llamó.

sw.L: Kila mmoja, katika wito ambao aliitwa, na akae katika huo.
sw.B: Kila mmoja wenu na aendelee katika nafasi ya maisha ambamo wito wa Mungu ulimkuta.
sw.R: Kila mmoja wenu abaki kama alivyokuwa Mungu alipomwita.

decisions.choice: calling: God's call, together with the situation in which it came
alternatives: the call itself: remain as one called
decisions.reason: κλήσει is God's act of calling (1:26). Here, with "remain in", it takes in the circumstances of the person when the call came: married or single, Jew or Gentile, slave or free. It does not yet have the later sense of a job or career.

decisions.choice: remain: go on in it, without striving to change it for God's sake
decisions.reason: μενέτω is the key word of verses 17-24. It is not an absolute ban on change: Paul has allowed for separation (verse 15) and may encourage a slave to take freedom (verse 21). The point is that no situation needs to be changed to please God.

decisions.choice: the place in life where God's call found you (B); as you were when God called you (R)
decisions.reason: In modern English "calling" usually means a career or a sense of vocation; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m1). Literal keeps "calling".

decisions.choice: {{gender:they were|he was}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: Each one means every believer, women and men.

decisions.choice: l’appel ... il a été appelé ... qu’il y demeure (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Vocation" now suggests a career, as "calling" does in English, so Literal says "l’appel", which keeps the link with "appeler". The pronouns after "chacun" are ordinary generic French and take no setting, unlike the English "they/he".

decisions.choice: fue llamado, permanezca, no gender span
decisions.reason: The Spanish verbs do not show whether "each one" is a man or a woman, as in 3:14, so the English gender spans ({{gender:they were|he was}}) have nothing to change in Spanish.

decisions.choice: llamamiento
decisions.reason: "Llamamiento" is God's call and keeps the link with "llamar" (called) in the same verse; "vocación" would suggest a career.

decisions.choice: aliitwa, akae: no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: The Swahili verb prefix a- means he or she, so the English gender spans have nothing to change.

source.text: Δοῦλος ἐκλήθης;

records.literal_gloss: A slave were you called?

en.L: Were you called [as a] slave?
en.B: Were you a slave when you were called?
en.R: Were you a slave when God called you?

fr.L: As-tu été appelé [étant] esclave ?
fr.B: Étais-tu esclave quand tu as été appelé ?
fr.R: Étais-tu esclave quand Dieu t’a appelé ?

es.L: ¿Fuiste llamado [siendo] esclavo?
es.B: ¿Eras esclavo cuando fuiste llamado?
es.R: ¿Eras esclavo cuando Dios te llamó?

sw.L: Uliitwa [ukiwa] mtumwa?
sw.B: Je, ulikuwa mtumwa ulipoitwa?
sw.R: Je, ulikuwa mtumwa Mungu alipokuita?

decisions.choice: slave: a person legally owned by another
decisions.reason: Slaves made up a large part of the population of Roman Corinth, and many belonged to the church (1:26-28). A slave was the owner's property; many were freed later in life. Paul speaks to them directly, as members of the church.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free (verses 21-23): the Greek word means one who was owned (m1), and the passage turns on that.

decisions.choice: esclave (every level, 7:21-23); tu
decisions.reason: As the English and the style guide: slave is set against free here, so "esclave" at every level. The Greek turns to a single reader, so French says "tu".

decisions.choice: esclavo at every level (verses 21-23)
decisions.reason: Slave is set against free in verses 21-23, so slavery itself is the point and every level keeps "esclavo", as the English does. Paul addresses one reader in the singular, "tú".

decisions.choice: mtumwa
decisions.reason: As the style guide and the English: slave set against free (verses 21-23), so "mtumwa" at every level, not "mtumishi".

source.text: μή σοι μελέτω· ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ δύνασαι ἐλεύθερος γενέσθαι, μᾶλλον χρῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Not to you let it be a care; but if even you are able free to become, rather make use.

en.L: Let it not concern you; but if indeed you are able to become free, rather make use [of it].
en.B: Do not let that worry you. But if you do get the chance to become free, make the most of it.
en.R: Do not worry about it. But if you have a chance to be set free, take it.

fr.L: Ne t’en soucie pas ; mais si tu peux aussi devenir libre, profites-en plutôt.
fr.B: Ne t’en inquiète pas. Mais si tu as l’occasion de devenir libre, saisis-la.
fr.R: Ne t’en fais pas pour cela. Mais si tu as la possibilité d’être libéré, profites-en.

es.L: No te preocupe; pero si también puedes llegar a ser libre, aprovéchalo más bien.
es.B: No dejes que eso te inquiete. Pero si se te presenta la oportunidad de ser libre, aprovéchala.
es.R: No te preocupes por eso. Pero si tienes la oportunidad de quedar libre, aprovéchala.

sw.L: Lisikusumbue; lakini hata kama unaweza kuwa huru, afadhali uitumie [nafasi hiyo].
sw.B: Usihangaike kwa hilo. Lakini ukipata nafasi ya kuwa huru, itumie vizuri.
sw.R: Usijali kuhusu hilo. Lakini ukipata nafasi ya kuachiliwa huru, ichukue.

decisions.choice: rather make use of it: take the opportunity to become free
alternatives: rather make use of your present state: stay a slave even if you could be freed
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "rather use", with no object. Read with ἀλλ ("but") and εἰ καὶ as "if indeed", it makes an exception to the rule of remaining: take freedom if it is offered. The aorist χρῆσαι suits seizing a particular chance. Read with εἰ καὶ as "even if", it means "even if you can be freed, rather make use of your slavery", which fits the repeated "remain" of verses 20 and 24. Both readings have long been held, and the evidence is evenly balanced.

decisions.choice: do not let it concern you: being a slave does not lower a person's standing with God
decisions.reason: μελέτω means to be a worry or concern. Verse 22 gives the reason: in the Lord a slave is the Lord's freed person.

decisions.choice: become free: be set free by one's owner
decisions.reason: In the Roman world many slaves were freed, by their owner's choice or by buying their freedom with their savings. A slave could not usually decide it alone, so Paul speaks of being "able" to become free.

decisions.choice: make the most of it (B); take it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading in m1 and say what is to be used: the chance of freedom. Literal keeps the Greek without an object.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ ἐν κυρίῳ κληθεὶς δοῦλος ἀπελεύθερος κυρίου ἐστίν· ὁμοίως ὁ ἐλεύθερος κληθεὶς δοῦλός ἐστιν Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The for in [the] Lord having been called slave a freedman of [the] Lord is; likewise the free having been called a slave is of Christ.

en.L: For the slave who was called in [the] Lord is [the] Lord's freedman; likewise the free [one] who was called is a slave of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: For a slave who has been called in the Lord is the Lord's freed slave; and in the same way, someone free who has been called is a slave of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: A slave whom God has called to belong to the Lord has been set free by the Lord. And a free person whom God has called has become a slave of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Car l’esclave qui a été appelé dans le Seigneur est un affranchi du Seigneur ; de même, celui qui a été appelé [étant] libre est un esclave du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
